deepdive.sec: AI & Data Science Solutions / AgeTech & LegalTech

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing internal product development (RELY, DocuXray); reducing new start-up investments unless exceptional; maintaining portfolio stakes (Mihup, Woovly, Pencil); Biome investing INR2Cr in OsteoForge; no dividend or buyback plans; cash burn being contained to achieve breakeven
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delayed conversion of pilots to revenue; regulatory uncertainty in AgeTech/EdTech; slow adoption of AI in Indian corporates; start-up ecosystem still fragile; dependence on few SaaS products for future revenue; ESOP dilution risk; SEBI ESM restrictions limiting market cap growth
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, patient, and execution-focused; acknowledges past start-up losses but emphasizes product-led turnaround; strong belief in RELY and DocuXray’s market validation; tone is optimistic on Q3/Q4FY26 revenue traction; dismisses short-term market cap concerns, framing it as a 7-10 year journey
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Mihup’s INR1B ARR is larger than Xelpmoc’s entire revenue; Xelpmoc’s true value lies in its portfolio of monetizing AI startups, not its own P&L; DocuXray’s per-document pricing model enables scalable, high-margin revenue without license constraints; OsteoForge’s silk-reinforced implant is India’s first of its kind, with potential for global IP licensing
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Startup engagements are monetised via cash+equity or pure equity (cost-plus equity model), effectively building an investee portfolio, while corporates are monetised in cash — the CEO frames shareholder exposure as 'more analogous to a leveraged mutual fund than a standard mutual fund.'
- Portfolio of 12 investee companies carried at a cumulative cost of Rs 79,803.72 thousand, with combined fair value of Rs 726.76 million as of June 30, 2026, up from Rs 531.85 million a year earlier.
- Active reinvestment into venture-studio holdings: Biome raising INR 8 Cr for Zoop.Money at ~INR 80 Cr valuation (4.4x uplift) and increasing its OsteoForge commitment to INR 4 Cr (versus an initially planned INR 2 Cr) for a 10% combined stake, after OsteoForge's valuation rose 2.5x to INR 100 Cr within five months.
- Shareholding as on June 30, 2026: Promoters 50.61%, Others 49.39%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: RELY (AgeTech): SaaS for assisted/independent senior living; deal size per apartment/month; pilot signings imminent; DocuXray (LegalTech): document automation framework for real estate, BFSI, insurance; priced per document processed; Mihup: AI voice analytics for customer service; clients: Tata Motors, HDFC Bank; Woovly: Live2.ai shoppable video SaaS; clients: L'Oreal, Titan; Pencil: AI-generated audio/books; contract with Alphabet; Snaphunt: recruitment marketplace; TSIM: LaaS for org excellence; Zoop.Money: white-label home loan platform; OsteoForge: resorbable ortho implant (INR2Cr investment)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xelpmoc’s revenue collapse due to start-up exit | Mihup | beneficiary | High | INR1B ARR, Tata Motors/HDFC Bank contracts; potential IPO by 2027-28 could unlock massive value for Xelpmoc shareholders |
| Low market cap due to ESM Stage 1 restrictions | Xelpmoc Design and Tech Limited | beneficiary | Medium | If RELY/DocuXray generate >INR50Cr revenue by FY27, SEBI may allow ESM exit, unlocking institutional interest |
| AI hype fatigue in corporate India | DocuXray | beneficiary | High | Pilots show 90%+ accuracy vs. ChatGPT; enterprise clients are paying for reliability, not buzz |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Operates a dual model: acts like a tech co-founder for startups under a cost-plus equity arrangement (earning equity akin to stock options), and as a cash-paid enabler/consultant for corporates doing end-to-end innovation projects rather than 'body shopping.'
- Investment Rationale slide: a differentiated technology-services play focused on Data Science, AI and ML, with the ability to identify unique business models and partner with entrepreneurs to bring ideas to fruition.
- XELP Network Ecosystem / 'Multidimensional Innovation Matrix': 1000+ corporate and startup connects plus an experienced, multi-faceted team, enabling faster innovation cycles and cross-application of solutions across the startup network.
- Stated vision is to partner and grow with start-ups while selectively working on traditional projects, prioritising shareholder value creation over a consistent traditional growth story.
- Global reach beyond India highlighted via 'Existing Ventures/Projects' and 'Prospective Engagements' sections, consistent with the Q1FY27 revenue geographic split skewed to International.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [RELY Commercial Launch] Flagship Agetech platform for the Assisted/Senior Living ecosystem went live in Q1FY27 with three customers onboarded, marking an important commercialisation milestone.
- [Portfolio traction] Mihup (conversation AI) reported Q1FY27 revenue of Rs 88.9 million with Rs 1,000+ million contracted value, a multi-million-dollar TML contract, and onboarded HDFC Bank; Woovly's ARR reached USD 4.3 million across 245+ brands.
- [Portfolio traction] Pencil signed a $950K, 36-month service deal with Alphabet/Google and has four AI-enabled products (audio, assessment, pitch bible, screenplay, proof-reading) due within 180 days (by Oct'26); The Star In Me (TSIM) won a Gold 'Startup of the Year' award at the ET Human Capital Annual Awards 2025.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Operating costs stable; EBITDA loss driven by revenue decline, not cost inflation; SaaS products (RELY, DocuXray) expected to yield 60-70% gross margins upon scale; start-up investments remain cash-burning; no cost-cutting beyond headcount stability (54 FTEs); R&D spend prioritized for product development
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: gradual traction expected from Q3FY26; margin: targeting EBITDA breakeven in next 1-2 quarters; order inflow: RELY pilots to convert to revenue by Q4FY26; DocuXray expanding to insurance/tech sectors; capex/commissioning: minimal; product development capex embedded in R&D; no new capex announced
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 2 active DocuXray clients; RELY in final stages of pilot signing (expected by Dec 2025); Mihup ARR INR1B; Woovly ARR USD3.2M; Pencil USD950K contract; TSIM revenue INR3Cr H1FY26
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: RELY expansion into home healthcare segment (Q3/Q4FY26); DocuXray replication in BFSI, insurance, accounting; international expansion of products (US/EU); potential IPO of Mihup by 2027-28; monetization of Biome’s portfolio (Zoop.Money fundraising INR8Cr at INR80Cr valuation); AI-generated content licensing (Pencil)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Xelpmoc has pivoted from start-up funding to monetizing its own AI-driven products—RELY (AgeTech) and DocuXray (LegalTech)—with pilot signings imminent and ARR from portfolio companies like Mihup (INR1B) and Woovly (USD3.2M) validating product-market fit; the shift from loss-making services to scalable SaaS is the key inflection point for profitability.
